title: PETA:Parameter-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Virtual Screening
abstract: arXiv:2608.19906v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurately ranking active ligands for a target protein pocket from massive chemical libraries remains a central challenge in virtual screening. DrugCLIP and its recent extensions substantially accelerate this process by encoding protein pockets and molecules into a shared embedding space. Despite this progress, further performance improvements typically require retraining the entire model, incurring substantial computational overhead and making target-specific customization inefficient. In this work, we formulate the specialization of pretrained virtual screening models to individual pockets as a test-time adaptation problem and propose PETA, a parameter-efficient framework that directly adapts pretrained model at test time. Given a target pocket, PETA constructs pocket-specific negatives through molecular diffusion and chemical validity filtering, and further moves them toward the reference ligand retrieved from structural databases via

translated_title: PETA：面向虚拟筛选的参数高效测试时自适应方法
translated_abstract: 摘要：从海量化合库中准确地对目标蛋白口袋的活性配体进行排序，仍然是虚拟筛选中的核心挑战。DrugCLIP及其近期扩展通过将蛋白口袋和分子编码到共享嵌入空间，大大加速了这一过程。尽管取得了这些进展，进一步的性能提升通常需要重新训练整个模型，这会导致巨大的计算开销，并使针对特定靶标的定制效率低下。在本工作中，我们将预训练虚拟筛选模型对单个口袋的特化问题形式化为测试时自适应任务，并提出PETA，一种参数高效的框架，可直接在测试时对预训练模型进行自适应。给定一个目标口袋，PETA通过分子扩散和化学有效性过滤构建口袋特异性的负样本，并进一步通过结构数据库检索到的参考配体将其移动。
tldr: 提出了一种名为PETA的参数高效测试时自适应框架，通过构建口袋特异性负样本并利用结构数据库参考配体，无需重训练即可实现对预训练虚拟筛选模型的靶标定制，显著提升效率。
en_tdlr: PETA proposes a parameter-efficient test-time adaptation framework that customizes pretrained virtual screening models to target pockets without retraining, using pocket-specific negatives and reference ligands from structural databases.
